brief.intent: RambleDesk desktop app Gate 1 direction B, Cryo Deck: use the spatial metaphor of the Vault Zero cryogenic deck to design an immersive, layered-glass cross-platform desktop UI while keeping the feedback document primary.
brief.audience: Power desktop users who accumulate voice, screenshot, file, clipboard, and written context without leaving their current workflow.
brief.emotionalGoal: Wake a task on a quiet cryogenic deck: cool light, order, and control, with gentle signs of life when Ramble is active.
brief.composition: 1536 by 1024 landscape desktop app. Beneath a custom titlebar, use three cabin-like columns: capsule request list on the left, a wide translucent archive-document bay in the center, and a vertical telemetry and Ramble status bay on the right; fixed submit/continue bar at bottom. Rambelle emerges naturally from the right status bay holding a transparent archive slate.
mustInclude: Cross-platform custom titlebar with drag region, project, online state, settings, and window controls
Capsule-like request queue, task steps, and context references
Largest area is a Tiptap-like rich feedback document with inline images
Start Ramble as a state transition, previewing audio level, screenshot, explicit clipboard import, and file import actions
Attachments, autosave, submit, and Feedback Package completed state
Cold silver-white, ice blue, and technical cyan with amber only for attention states
New hexagonal vault-door motif and cryo indicator lights; readable Simplified Chinese labels
avoid: Dark-dominant background, strong neon, or glitch
Old circular zero emblem or eye-like symbol
Oversized character art that crowds the editor

acceptanceCriteria: Immersive spatial feeling while remaining implementable productivity UI
Rich document has highest visual weight
Ramble status and multimodal entries are recognizable at a glance
Titlebar and three-column structure are clear and cross-platform
No old emblem or excessive cyberpunk decoration
notes: RepoChan Web Designer Gate 1 visual direction B. L4 content stays live; glass and lighting are reproducible CSS layers.
